# SPD-008 — Enforcement hooks: Laws 3, 4, 6, 7, the path rule, the finishing rule, spawn recording

## Brief
Implement the hook table in the spike's Enforcement plan ([[SPD-006]], `docs/spikes/2026-09-12-ledger-database.md`): `PreToolUse(Agent)`, `PostToolUse(Agent)`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreToolUse(Bash)`, `PreToolUse(Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit)`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`, each `python3.14 -I -S $SPUD_HOME/bin/spud hook <name>`, installed into `.claude/settings.json` by `spud settings sync` together with the `permissions.allow` rule for the CLI. Enforcing hooks fail closed (exit 2 with the reason); recording hooks fail open and write a `hook.error` event afterwards. `agent_id` binds to a member through `tool_use_id`.

Two corrections from Spud's review of the spike: (1) direct database access is refused for writes only; read-only queries stay allowed, or the CLI offers `spud sql --readonly`, so the inspection path the spike promises Spud still works inside a session; (2) Spud's writable paths include `ledger/Home.md`, `ledger/Spud.md` and the `.base` files, which the Migration plan keeps hand-written.

Depends on [[SPD-007]]. Decided by Eric, 2026-09-12: both spawn-convention changes are approved, descriptions carry the team key and every spudagent spawn defaults to `run_in_background: true` (question 5); enforcement refuses from day one, including the path rule and the finishing hold (question 6). The fan-out check counts children alive at once (question 3).

Done when: each hook is installed and exercised by a headless `claude -p` run like the spike's probes; a spawn without a planned row, a spawn without a model, a spudagent `git commit`, and a write outside a member's deliverables are each refused with a reason; a child returning without a Result is held once; the ledger records every spawn with its usage.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer lead. **Tier override: fable instead of opus.** Reason: enforcement is security-adjacent and the failure mode is silent (a hook that fails open on a law). The lead may add a reviewer on fable (`01.01`) to attack the hooks before returning, as SPD-007 did; the brief asks for it. Spud's resolutions of the two corrections, written into the brief: direct database access is refused in Bash for everyone and inspection goes through a new `spud sql --readonly`; Spud's hand-written set is `spud.config.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `docs/superpowers/specs/**`, `ledger/Home.md`, `ledger/Spud.md`, `ledger/*.base`, `ledger/_templates/**`. A missing database makes enforcing hooks refuse (the hooks are installed only at cutover, after `spud init`). Code on branch `worktree-spd-008-enforcement-hooks`; the live `.claude/settings.json` is not touched until cutover.

## Outcome
Shipped on branch `worktree-spd-008-enforcement-hooks` (commit df50df1, pushed; worktree kept at `.claude/worktrees/spd-008-enforcement-hooks`) by [[SPUD-008/Desiree|Desiree]] (01, engineer, fable), reviewed by [[SPUD-008/Rooster|Rooster]] (01.01, reviewer, fable): `bin/spud` from 2,898 to 4,430 lines. `spud hook <event>` for `PreToolUse` (dispatching on `tool_name` to Agent, Bash and Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit), `PostToolUse` (Agent), `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`. Enforcing hooks (`PreToolUse`, `Stop`) fail closed: a planned refusal is `permissionDecision: deny` with the law's number and the fix in the reason, any exception is exit 2; recording hooks fail open and spool the gap into `<SPUD_HOME>/.spud/hook-errors.jsonl`, drained into `hook.error` events by the next hook or CLI command. The first `PreToolUse(Agent)` allow reserves the planned row (Rooster's HIGH-1); `PostToolUse(Agent)` binds by `tool_use_id`; a foreground child is bound at its first tool call from the harness's `agent-<id>.meta.json`, a meta binding only when its description and agent type match the request; the oldest-unbound fallback binds only when unambiguous. `ledger/` and `reports/` are protected whatever the case (this Mac's filesystem is case-insensitive, Rooster's HIGH-2); Spud's hand-written set is `spud.config.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `docs/superpowers/specs/**`, `ledger/Home.md`, `ledger/Spud.md`, `ledger/*.base`, `ledger/_templates/**`. The Bash hook refuses, for members, git writes behind every shell construct including substitution-produced command words, `--as` for anyone but the caller's own bound member, Spud-only commands, `spud hook`, and database access for everyone; well-formed `spud` calls get `permissionDecision: allow`. `spud settings sync` writes the eight hook entries (`SPUD_HOME=<home> <python> -I -S <home>/bin/spud hook <event>`, timeout 30 s) and three allow rules, merged and idempotent. `spud sql --readonly` (mode=ro, `query_only`, one read statement) is the inspection path. `--as` and `--json` are accepted anywhere on the line.

Verified: Spud's run at df50df1, `Ran 207 tests in 89.052s` / `OK` (124 from SPD-007, 83 new), no bytecode, no `.spud/` at the ledger root, live `.claude/settings.json` untouched. Seven headless `claude -p` probes (2.1.269, haiku, scratch homes, settings generated by `settings sync`, about $1.30 in total) show: no planned row → refused with Law 2; no model → refused with Law 3, then allowed with `model: haiku`; a child's `git commit` → refused with Law 7; a Write outside the member's globs → refused with Law 5, a write inside created, foreground and background; every child returning without a Result held once, then let go after `spud --as <id> member result`; every spawn recorded with `agent_id`, resolved model and usage; the `Stop` hook blocking Spud's turn once with the Law 9 list; the hook's own allow letting a background child run `spud` with no allow rule. Hook latency about 60 ms per call (SPD-016). Rooster's attack matrix, everything else held, in his file.

Corrections to the spike, from today's docs: `totalTokens`/`usage` on `PostToolUse(Agent)` cover the final request only; `SessionStart` also fires for `clear` and `fork`; permission rules are documented as `Bash(cmd *)` with `:*` equivalent; `Agent(model:…)` and `Agent(isolation:…)` rules exist natively; hook `timeout` is seconds; `meta.json` exists about one second after the spawn.

Left: cutover is Eric's go, as a separate step: `spud init`, `import`, `render`, one commit, then `spud settings sync` on the live `/Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/.claude/settings.json`; at cutover confirm no v1 database exists anywhere, because the events trigger was amended in schema v1 without a `0002` migration. Merging the branch is Eric's call. [[SPD-009]] rewrites the protocol around these commands (inputs listed on that ticket). [[SPD-015]], [[SPD-016]], [[SPD-017]] hold the follow-ups.
